explanation: The cornea has no blood vessels, which keeps it clear. Oxygen from the air dissolves into the film of tears covering it; with the eyes shut, the eyelids supply it instead.

claims.text: The cornea gets most of its oxygen directly from the air, dissolved through the tear film, rather than from blood vessels.
The eardrum, the tongue and the lips have blood vessels that supply their oxygen.
The cornea has no blood vessels, which helps keep it transparent.
When the eyes are closed, the cornea gets oxygen from blood vessels in the inner lining of the eyelids.
